properties.biography: Anders Trentemøller began performing in 1997 as part of Trigbag, one of Denmark's early live-house acts. After Trigbag disbanded in 2000, he returned to solo production and released The Trentemøller EP in 2003, earning national recognition (including the Danish DJ Awards for “Le Champagne”). Releases on Audiomatique and Poker Flat through the mid-2000s — plus high-profile remixes and an acclaimed Essential Mix — propelled him to international attention. His debut double-album The Last Resort (2006) won widespread critical praise; he continued evolving toward song-based, midtempo and cinematic work with Into The Great Wide Yonder (2010) and Lost (2013). Trentemøller balances club-oriented singles with full-band live shows and guest vocalists, running his In My Room imprint and maintaining an influential presence in European electronic music.
properties.known_for: Creating atmospheric, cinematic electronic productions that blend minimal techno, ambient textures and song-based arrangements; acclaimed remixes and immersive live shows.
properties.description: Anders Trentemøller is a Danish electronic music producer and multi-instrumentalist from Copenhagen. Trentemøller's work blends minimal techno, ambient and indie songwriting into atmospheric, cinematic compositions; he is also a sought-after remixer and has collaborated with numerous vocalists and producers. Notable albums include The Last Resort (2006), Into The Great Wide Yonder (2010), Lost (2013) and Fixion (2016).
properties.cultural_impact: Trentemøller helped bridge minimal/techno dance culture and song-oriented, cinematic electronic music in Europe, influencing a generation of producers who blend club aesthetics with indie songwriting; his remixes and albums received critical accolades and established Denmark as a notable presence in modern electronic music.
